page.layout: One printed page of running text in a single column, framed by a decorative woodcut border; page number and running head at the top; catchword at the foot right. A partial page of text on the right edge of the scan belongs to the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: Ferrariensi physico & chymico in eorum operibus præscripta, & quæcunque præterea ad veri auri naturalis proprietates examinandas adhiberi debent, ut sunt Ignitio, Fusio, sub malleo per omnem dimensionem Extensio, Cineritium, Expositio super vapores acutos, & per aquam Regalem Solutio, Extinctio, Cementum, Commixtio rei adurentis, post calcinationem Reductio, Susceptio argtēi vivi facilis vel difficilis &c. Si igitur ad omne specillum probatum aurum fiat, nec ut sophisticatum perdatur, sed substet, habens omnes proprietates auri naturalis, omnes operationes & passiones (quale nostrum esse dicimus) non simile, sed idem cum naturali erit, quicquid deliret cum Ægidio Pererius. Nam quod de serpentibus & draconculis à Magis & Mose factum affertur, illorum fuit diabolicæ illusionis, hujus à divina virtute. page.notes: Printed "argtēi" is probably "argenti" with a damaged or misprinted abbreviation; "Pererius" and "Ægidio" as printed. The catchword "pu." is partly visible at the foot right. Marginal numerals on the right edge belong to the neighbouring page. The gloss mark "3" after "quæcunque" is a stray printed mark and is not transcribed as text.
